acts.applicability: All states of India (with some state amendments)

sections.title: Transfer of Property defined
sections.description: In the following sections 'transfer of property' means an act by which a living person conveys property, in present or in future, to one or more other living persons, or to himself, or to himself and one or more other living persons. 'Living person' includes a company or association or body of individuals.

sections.title: Sale defined
sections.description: Sale is a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised. Such transfer, in the case of tangible immoveable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, can be made only by a registered instrument.

sections.title: Rights and Liabilities of Buyer and Seller
sections.description: In the absence of a contract to the contrary, the buyer and seller of immoveable property are subject to liabilities and have rights as detailed. Seller must disclose defects, buyer must pay price.

sections.title: Mortgage and Mortgagee defined
sections.description: A mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immoveable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt.

sections.title: Mortgage when to be by assurance
sections.description: Where the principal money secured is one hundred rupees or upwards, a mortgage can be effected only by a registered instrument signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses.

sections.title: Power of Sale
sections.description: A mortgagee, or any person acting on his behalf, shall, subject to the provisions of this section, have power to sell or concur in selling the mortgaged property in default of payment of the mortgage-money.

sections.title: Lease Defined
sections.description: A lease of immoveable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value.

sections.title: Duration of Certain Leases
sections.description: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immoveable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice; a lease of immoveable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month.

sections.title: Rights and Liabilities of Lessor and Lessee
sections.description: In the absence of a contract to the contrary, the lessor and lessee of immoveable property have rights and are subject to liabilities: lessor must give possession and disclose defects; lessee must pay rent, not use for other purposes, keep premises in good repair.

sections.title: Gift defined
sections.description: Gift is the transfer of certain existing moveable or immoveable property made voluntarily and without consideration, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and accepted by or on behalf of the donee.

sections.title: Transfer how effected (Gift)
sections.description: For the purpose of making a gift of immoveable property, the transfer must be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor, and attested by at least two witnesses.

sections.title: Documents of which registration is compulsory
sections.description: The following documents shall be registered: instruments of gift of immoveable property; other non-testamentary instruments which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any right, title or interest to or in immoveable property, where the value is Rs. 100 and upwards; leases of immoveable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year.

sections.title: Documents of which registration is optional
sections.description: Any of the following documents may be registered under this Act, namely: instruments (other than instruments of gift and wills) which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any right, title or interest to or in immoveable property where the value is less than one hundred rupees.

sections.title: Effect of non-registration of documents required to be registered
sections.description: No document required by section 17 shall affect any immoveable property or be received as evidence of any transaction affecting such property, unless it has been registered.

acts.applicability: All states and Union Territories of India

sections.title: Prior Registration of Real Estate Project with Real Estate Regulatory Authority
sections.description: No promoter shall advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale, or invite persons to purchase in any manner any plot, apartment or building, in any real estate project or part of it, in any planning area, without registering the real estate project with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority.

sections.title: Functions and Duties of Promoter
sections.description: The promoter shall make available to the allottees at the time of booking and issue of allotment letter all information including sanctioned plans, layout plans, stage wise time schedule of completion, specifications, amenities, facilities, details of encumbrances.

sections.title: No deposit or advance to be taken without first entering into agreement for sale
sections.description: A promoter shall not accept a sum more than ten per cent of the cost of the apartment, plot, or building as an advance payment or an application fee, from a person without first entering into a written agreement for sale with such person.

sections.title: Return of Amount and Compensation
sections.description: If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale, the promoter shall be liable to return all amounts received with interest and compensation.

sections.title: Rights and Duties of Allottees
sections.description: Every allottee shall be entitled to obtain information relating to sanctioned plans, layout plans along with the specifications; claim possession of apartment; claim refund of amount paid along with interest if promoter defaults; have the right to claim compensation.

sections.title: Filing of Complaints with Real Estate Regulatory Authority
sections.description: Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer for any violation or contravention of the provisions of this Act.

sections.title: Recovery of Interest, Penalty, Compensation etc.
sections.description: Any amount payable under this Act, including interest, penalty, and compensation, shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

acts.applicability: All of India (state amendments apply for stamp duty rates)

sections.title: Instruments chargeable with duty
sections.description: Subject to the provisions of this Act and the exemptions contained in Schedule I, the following instruments shall be chargeable with duty of the amount indicated in that Schedule: every instrument mentioned in that Schedule which, not having been previously executed by any person, is executed in India.

sections.title: Stamp Duty on Sale Deed
sections.description: Stamp duty on sale deed varies by state: Karnataka: 5% + 1% registration fee; Maharashtra: 5% + 1% Local Body Tax; Tamil Nadu: 7% + 4% registration; Delhi: 4% for women, 6% for men; Telangana: 4% + 0.5% transfer duty.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.description: In this Act, 'affected family' means any family whose land or other immoveable property has been acquired; 'appropriate Government' means, in relation to acquisition of land situated within the territory of a State, the State Government.

sections.title: Determination of Market Value of Land by Collector
sections.description: The Collector shall adopt the higher of the following criteria for determining the value of land: the market value fixed by the appropriate Government; or the average of the sale price for similar type of land situated in the vicinity, ascertained from the highest fifty per centum of sale deeds.

sections.title: Social Impact Assessment
sections.description: Whenever a State Government intends to acquire land for a public purpose, it shall carry out a Social Impact Assessment study in consultation with the concerned Panchayat, Municipality or Municipal Corporation.
